card: Makes files opened with fsbridge::fopen non-inheritable across exec calls by automatically passing 'e' on POSIX and 'N' on Windows fopen mode strings. This prevents file descriptors from leaking into child processes spawned by Bitcoin Core. The change cites standard non-inheritance modes across operating systems, with no linked issue or external bug report provided.
evidence: Author's commit and description: "Use the 'e' mode on POSIX to set close-on-exec and the 'N' mode on windows to prevent file handle inheritance by child processes."
problem: File descriptors and handles opened through fsbridge::fopen can remain inheritable across process boundaries, potentially leaking open files into spawned child processes.

risk.why: If a platform C library does not support the extra mode character, fopen calls could fail to open files or behave unexpectedly.

scope_notes: The diff was not provided in the input, but the PR appears to touch fsbridge wrapper functions and add unit tests.
summary: Sets close-on-exec and non-inheritable flags by default for files opened via fsbridge::fopen. On POSIX systems, it appends the 'e' mode character, and on Windows, it appends the 'N' mode character to the fopen mode string.
uncertainties: The diff was omitted from the input, so platform-specific compatibility handling (e.g., whether all targeted POSIX libcs support 'e') cannot be inspected.
